question.text: Let the point, on the line passing through the points $P(1,-2,3)$ and $Q(5,-4,7)$, farther from the origin and at distance of 9 units from the point $\mathrm{P}$, be $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$. Then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is equal to :

solution.text:
$P Q$ line
$\begin{aligned}
& \frac{x-1}{4}=\frac{y+2}{-2}=\frac{z-3}{4} \\
& \operatorname{pt}(4 t+1,-2 t-2,4 t+3) \\
& \text { distance }{ }^2=16 t^2+4 t^2+16 t^2=81 \\
& t= \pm \frac{3}{2} \\
& \operatorname{pt}(7,-5,9) \\
& \alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=155
\end{aligned}$
